title: §7 item 60 — the death case: which answers should go into the bill?
summary: Store revision 40 is written and the death case's benefit measure is the one thing left, and it is a policy choice. Five answers are drafted in full and none is enacted. Any combination is available. Check what you want drafted in; reject if you want to discuss first.

payload.prompt: Check each answer you want enacted in the next revision of bill-text-s8. Any combination; none is also an answer.
payload.detailsMarkdown:
Full text of all five in `moo118-disposition` §3 and at §7 item 60 of `bill-text-s8`. MOO-118's three serious findings are one question: what the survivor's benefit is measured on. Frequency bound 0.1013 expected deaths in the window — severe in law, about a one-in-ten event in fact.

**(d) is the only answer that closes all three serious findings at once**, and taking it deletes about 700 characters of store revision 40's own enumeration as surplusage, which is the right trade. It also forecloses the survivor's argument that she was promised an *unreduced* allowance. I will not pick one: three of these four paragraphs are about who bears a loss.

options.label: (a) Preserve the elected option — the narrow bridge
options.description: Names § 51.1-165 in order to displace it, so it partly reverses MOO-96's F-4. Reaches the contingent annuitant who is not a spouse, minor child or parent. Increases the trust's liability in the cases it reaches; unpriced.

options.label: (b) Cap what the Commonwealth settles
options.description: Does nothing unless it expressly disapplies the certified-subsidy floor — and disapplying the floor moves the loss from the appropriation to the trust fund, engaging Va. Const. art. X, § 11 and the § 30-19.1:7 statement.

options.label: (c) Extend G 4's employer refund to the case the credit produced nothing
options.description: The only one of the five that compensates a named loser (the employing agency that paid 95% under subdivision B 4 e). An addition, so it is yours. Does not answer the 'paying for nothing' objection.

options.label: (d) NEW ON PASS 13 — name the measure
options.description: One sentence: the benefit payable is the benefit the chapter provides on the death of a member in service, computed on the service credit credited under this subdivision. Closes F1, F2 and F3 at once; names no section; makes the 'as though' hypothetical and store revision 40's enumeration surplusage.

options.label: (e) NEW ON PASS 13 — the partial-payment measure, whole
options.description: Two clauses inside G 4's fourth sentence: the service base, plus subdivision G 3's unreduced-date guard which G 4's partial-payer branch lacks. Must go whole — either half alone repeats MOO-104's fatal error. (d) subsumes its first half.

options.label: Also answer MOO-118's F8 — a notice duty in the full-payment death case
options.description: G 4's written-notice duty sits in the partial-payment branch only, so a full-payment death carries no notice duty at all. Declined as an unagreed new duty on the Board; check this and I will draft it.

title: §7 item 60 after (d): the elected-option class is now worse off, and (a) is the only answer that reaches it
summary: (d) and F8's notice are enacted in store revision 45. Five drafted answers remain; check any combination, or none.

payload.prompt: Check each answer you want drafted into the next revision of bill-text-s8. Any combination; none is also an answer.
payload.detailsMarkdown:
**(d) is enacted in store revision 45 of [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8), and it did exactly what it said it would do — and it leaves one class worse off than before, which is why this card exists rather than a note in the record.**

(d) now says, in subdivision G 4: *"The benefit payable under this subdivision shall be the benefit this chapter provides on the death of a member in service, computed on the service credit credited under this subdivision."* That is a **measure**, and it is the one the Board would have had to use anyway. But it **names no section**, so it does not touch **§ 51.1-165 C 1**, which provides that *"in all cases"* where a member dies before her effective date of retirement **but after the Board has her written notification of it**, benefits are paid under **§ 51.1-163** — a refund of her own contributions — unless § 51.1-165 C 2's spouse, minor child or parent saves her.

**Subdivision D 1 compels that filing within 30 days.** So the bill requires the act that triggers the refund routing, and (d) now confirms the chapter's answer rather than overriding it. Before this revision a survivor could at least argue that the deleted deeming had made her member a retiree on the date of death and that her elected option took effect. **That argument is gone.** The class that loses is the member who elected an option under § 51.1-165 naming a contingent annuitant who is **not** a spouse, minor child or parent — a sibling, an adult child, an unmarried partner.

**Nothing below is in the bill.** Each is drafted in full at §7 item 60 of [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8) with its cost stated. Check any combination; none is also an answer. The first three are the three I would not pick for you, because each of them decides **who bears a loss**.


**One option from the last card is withdrawn rather than carried forward.** (e)'s remaining half — importing subdivision G 3's guard into G 4 — is **unnecessary**, and that corrects a premise of mine: the last sentence of **subsection E** already provides that no member is treated as having reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date by reason of an election before payment in full is received, and a member who dies before completing payment has not paid in full. **Nothing is lost by not taking it.**

options.label: (a) Preserve the elected option — the narrow bridge
options.description: One sentence displacing § 51.1-165 C where the member had elected an option before death, so the benefit is determined as though she had retired under the option she chose. The only answer that reaches the class above. Cost: it names a section in order to displace it, a partial reversal of MOO-96's F-4, and it increases the trust's liability in the cases it reaches.

options.label: (b) Cap what the Commonwealth settles, and disapply the subsidy floor
options.description: Settles the lesser of the redetermined amount, the amount reserved, and the actuarial increase the credit actually produced — and it must expressly disapply the 'certified subsidy' floor or it does nothing. Cost: it moves the loss from the appropriation to the trust fund, engaging Va. Const. art. X, § 11 and the § 30-19.1:7 impact statement.

options.label: (c) Refund the employer where the credit produced nothing
options.description: Where a death settlement produces no increase in the actuarial present value of benefits, the Board refunds the employer what it paid under subdivision B 4 e, in 60 days. The only answer that compensates a named loser. Cost: it is an addition, and it does not answer the 'paying for nothing' objection.

options.label: Give the Board a date by which it must credit in the death case
options.description: The new 30-day notice duty runs from the crediting, and G 4 sets no date by which the Board must credit when a member dies — so the duty is bounded in content and not in time. A deadline is a new duty on the Board and is yours, not mine. Smallest form: 60 days after the Board learns of the death.

options.label: Amend subsection M 2 to reach the estate and the personal representative
options.description: Item 61's third answer, now load-bearing in a second place: the new notice tells the estate it may seek review under subsection M, and M 2 reaches only 'a member, retiree, or beneficiary'. One sentence adds the applicant and the personal representative of a deceased member.

result.reason: Superseded. MOO-126 rated this card's subject FATAL and corrected two of its premises: the class harmed by § 51.1-165 C 1 is a member survived by a spouse, minor child or parent who elected no option — not the elected-option class this card named — and option (a) grants a benefit rather than restoring one. A replacement card with that correction, a new option (f), and seven further drafted answers is posted in its place.

title: MOO-126 is FATAL on the death case. Nine drafted answers, none enacted — and two corrections that change which one to prefer
summary: § 51.1-165 C 1 routes the compelled-notice death to a refund of the member's own contributions. Nine answers are drafted in full; check any combination, or none.

payload.prompt: Check each answer you want drafted into the next revision of bill-text-s8. Any combination; none is also an answer.
payload.detailsMarkdown:
**[MOO-126](/MOO/issues/MOO-126) returned a FATAL finding against text the last card put into the bill, and the answer is yours. Every option below is drafted word for word, with its cost, at [`moo126-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-97#document-moo126-disposition) §7.**

**The chain, on the face of the act.** **Subdivision D 1 compels** the member to file her § 51.1-153 notice of retirement within 30 days of the Board's statement. **§ 51.1-165 C 1** then provides that *"in all cases"* where death occurs before the effective date but after the Board has that notification, benefits are paid under **§ 51.1-163** — a refund of her own contributions. **§ 51.1-165 C 2** rescues only a member who elected a joint and last-survivor option naming a spouse, minor child or parent, an election the bill never requires, prompts or discloses. Store revision 45 deleted the deeming that had made C 1's gateway arguable, so **what was arguable is now settled, and the live text is worse for one class than store revision 41 was.**

**Two corrections to the last card, and they change which answer is worth buying.** **One — § 51.1-162 B pays an allowance only to *"the member's (i) surviving spouse, (ii) minor child, or (iii) parent(s)"*.** So the class that actually loses a benefit is **a member survived by one of those three who elected no option** — she loses a § 51.1-162 B allowance the purchased credit would have increased. A member with none of those three takes a refund either way, and the credit buys her survivors nothing on either route; that is what Chapter 1 does for anyone in her position, not a defect this bill created. **Two, and this corrects me: (a) is not a bridge.** A contingent annuitant who is a sibling, an adult child or an unmarried partner is reached by **no** provision of § 51.1-162, so (a) **grants** a benefit rather than restoring one.

**Nothing below is in the bill, and none of it is enacted.** The two repairs this pass did make — the notice's employer class and its circular addressee — are cut as store revision 47 and are waiting on a document lock; they do not touch any of this.

**I will not pick for you.** Three of these options decide **who bears a loss**. The one place I have named a default is option 7, because it is a procedural right rather than a distributive question.

options.label: (f) NEW — keep a death in service a death in service
options.description: Notwithstanding subdivision C 1 of § 51.1-165, the compelled D 1 filing does not route the death to § 51.1-163, and the Board determines the benefit under § 51.1-162 as on a death in service. The answer that reaches the class above, and it supplies the missing priority rule for a workers'-comp death. Cost: three sections named, the fullest reversal of MOO-96's F-4 on this card; unpriced new trust liability; and it SUPERSEDES (d), the sentence you approved last card.

options.label: (a) Preserve the elected option — unchanged, and now correctly described
options.description: One sentence displacing § 51.1-165 C where the member had elected an option before death, so the benefit is determined as though she retired under the option she chose. It is the only option that reaches a non-spouse contingent annuitant — whom (f) does not help, because § 51.1-162 does not reach them either. Cost: it grants a benefit Chapter 1 does not give on a death in service, and it names a section to displace one.

options.label: (b) Cap what the Commonwealth settles, and disapply the subsidy floor
options.description: Settles the least of the redetermined amount, the amount reserved, and the actuarial increase the credit actually produced — and it must expressly disapply the 'certified subsidy' floor or it does nothing. It is also the drafted answer to MOO-126's F7, the redetermination that values a retirement which did not occur. Cost: it moves the loss from the appropriation to the trust fund, engaging Va. Const. art. X, § 11 and the § 30-19.1:7 impact statement.

options.label: (c) Refund the employer where the credit produced nothing
options.description: Where a death settlement produces no increase in the actuarial present value of benefits, the Board refunds the employer what it paid under subdivision B 4 e, within 60 days. The only option that compensates a named loser rather than re-routing a trust-fund entry. Cost: it is an addition, and it does not answer the 'paying for nothing' objection — it answers the 'and the agency lost its money' one.

options.label: Tell the member what the option election is worth BEFORE she files (the only free answer to the fatal finding)
options.description: One sentence into subdivision D 1: the Board must state that a death after filing and before the effective date is governed by § 51.1-165 C, and that a joint and last-survivor option naming her spouse, minor child or parent is the only election that preserves an allowance for that person. No new remedy is needed — D 1 already extends her final date day for day for a late statement. Cost: no money; it discloses that the compelled filing can cost her family an allowance.

options.label: The three remaining disclosure and reporting repairs, as a set
options.description: (1) Notice to a claimant the Board considered and rejected, with the review clock running from notice to that person — MOO-126's F4, live half. (2) Notice of the survivor's own § 51.1-162 rights and their deadlines, including the 90-day waiver whose lapse forfeits a larger allowance — F2 and F3. (3) The subsection J reporting hook for a death notice the Board fails to give — F8's missing half. All three are duties on the Board with no fiscal effect. Reject with a note if you want only some.

options.label: Subsection M standing for the member's estate (I have named a default)
options.description: M 2 reaches 'a member, retiree, beneficiary, or applicant'. The ESTATE, which is who the refund is paid to, is not in that list — so the one addressee that receives money is the one whose promised review is doubtful. Form 1, which I will draft unless you say otherwise, adds 'personal representative of a deceased member's estate' to M 2. Form 2 makes the limb self-executing; Form 3 withdraws the promise. Doing nothing leaves enacted words promising a review that may not be honoured.

options.label: Give the Board a date by which it must credit in the death case
options.description: Subsection E dates the crediting only for the ordinary case and expressly carves the death case out of its own rule, so the 30-day notice clock and the subsection M clock hang off an undated event — while settlement runs from the date of death and subsection N then compels payment. The money moves on a clock the family's notice does not have. Smallest form: 60 days after the Board learns of the death. Cost: a new duty with a numeral that is mine unless you move it.

options.label: Release the settled subsidy where the survivor takes the contributions instead
options.description: Where a survivor elects accumulated contributions 'in lieu of any other benefits' under § 51.1-162 B, the credit buys nothing, yet the subsidy is paid under subsection N and stays charged against the $3,000,000 cap for good. This releases it and restores the cap. No amendment to D 2 is needed — its own words already permit a release required by G 4. At the central $94,649 that is one further election's worth of cap. Cost: it takes money back from the system after settlement.

title: Store revision 58 is in: nine drafted answers from MOO-154, four of which decide who bears a loss
summary: The fatal finding is cured and eleven findings are enacted. These nine are drafted and not enacted. Check any combination; see the three alternation notes.

payload.prompt: Check each answer you want drafted into the bill.
payload.detailsMarkdown:
**Store revision 58 is in the text and cures [MOO-154](/MOO/issues/MOO-154)'s fatal finding.** Eleven of its sixteen findings are enacted, two are declined as nulls with reasons, and **these nine are drafted word for word and enacted nowhere** — because four of them decide who bears a loss, and that is not mine to decide. Each is one substitution. Every word of each is at [`moo154-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-97#document-moo154-disposition) §8.

**Check any combination; I will draft exactly what you check.** Three notes before you do.

- **(1) F5 is the one I would put first.** It is the ERF residual this issue was opened on, and it is the only item where **the Commonwealth is already paying for an outcome the text may not deliver**: the certified subsidy is priced on the member's *unreduced* retirement, and subsection E's second limb may leave her survivor the *reduced* allowance. **Forms A and B are alternatives — check at most one.** A costs more; B leaves the partial payer reduced, and the partial payer is the case the branch was written for. The figure is Fiscal's and neither form is priced.
- **(2)(i) and (2)(ii) are alternatives — check at most one**, and **(2)(ii) should not be enacted without counsel on Va. Const. art. X, § 11**, because it takes money back out of the trust fund after settlement. **Doing nothing on (2) is a decision**: the $3,000,000 cap then bounds reservations and not Commonwealth cash, and that must go in the fiscal note and the memo.
- **(4) widens what the cap gives back, so it works against (2).** Decide them together.

**Not on this card and still open:** §7 item 60's (a), (b) and (c) — the elected-option class whose contingent annuitant is a sibling, an adult child or an unmarried partner. (f) routes her death to § 51.1-162, and § 51.1-162 B pays only a spouse, minor child or parent. She remains unanswered and MOO-154 does not change that.

**Internal working draft throughout. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill, not reviewed by DLS, not legally sufficient for introduction.**

options.label: (1) F5 Form A — the unreduced allowance for every G 4 death the credit carries over the line
options.description: Extends G 4's saving so subsection E's second limb cannot leave the survivor a reduced allowance. Alternative to Form B. Costs the most of the nine; unpriced.

options.label: (1) F5 Form B — the unreduced allowance only where the member completed payment before death
options.description: Same cure, confined to the full payer. Alternative to Form A. Leaves the partial payer reduced.

options.label: (2)(i) Restore to the cap only so much of a settled amount as has NOT been paid under subsection N
options.description: Keeps the cap a limit on Commonwealth cash; gives the Program back less capacity than the current words promise. Alternative to (2)(ii).

options.label: (2)(ii) Recover the cash — the retirement system repays the appropriation within 60 days
options.description: Takes money back out of the trust fund after settlement. MOO-96's F-3 and Va. Const. art. X, § 11 both bear on it; I would not enact it without counsel on that point. Alternative to (2)(i).

options.label: (3) F9(b) — reinstate a released settled amount where the determination is reversed on review
options.description: Today a survivor who wins her reconsideration or judicial review has nothing left to be paid out of: the once-only settlement rule bars re-settling and the reinstatement machinery only reaches released reservations.

options.label: (4) F10/F11 — trigger the release where NO allowance is payable, instead of on an election
options.description: Cures the unmarried member who frees nothing, and the two-minor-children case where one guardian elects while an allowance is still payable to the other. Widens what the cap gives back; interacts with (2).

options.label: (5) F12 alternative — state a 90-day period in G 4 for the § 51.1-162 election, and run the release from its expiry
options.description: § 51.1-162 B states no period; the 90 days is § 51.1-162 C's figure. Closes (2)'s open-ended driver and takes a right from a survivor who is slow. The numeral would be mine.

options.label: (6) F13(c) — a 30-day duty on the employing state agency to tell the Board of the death, with a subsection J line
options.description: The crediting deadline runs from when the Board 'learns of' the death and nothing requires anyone to tell it. Drafted on G 4's own involuntary-separation model. Confined to state agencies: a duty on a local employer needs an express grant.

options.label: (7) F13(e) — run the 90-day redetermination from the date the Board learns of the death, in the death case
options.description: Today it runs from the date of death, so where the Board learns late the deadline has already expired. Only ever moves the deadline later.

options.label: (8) F15 — name a payee for the refund where no personal representative of the estate has qualified
options.description: G 4 pays a refund 'to the member's estate' and nothing requires an estate to be opened. Drafted to pay and notify the person who received the accumulated contributions under § 51.1-162. It names a payee, which is why it is yours.

options.label: (9) F1 alternative — displace § 51.1-165 C 2 instead of preserving it
options.description: What is enacted pays the greater of C 2's benefit and (f)'s, so no member is worse off than under present law. This is 230 characters shorter and takes an existing right from a spouse, minor child or parent under a joint and last-survivor option.
